```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
options(width = 72)
has_delarr <- requireNamespace("delarr", quietly = TRUE) &&
  utils::packageVersion("delarr") >= "0.2.0"
note <- function(pkg) {
  cat(
    '<p class="chunk-note">The next chunk needs the <code>', pkg,

    sep = ""

```

*This vignette is for authors of packages that store fMRI arrays in a new
format. You do not need it to analyse data.*

Every assay in a frame is backed by an *array source*: a small, serializable
description of a two-dimensional array, plus methods that read from it. The
package ships in-memory, NIfTI, and experimental Zarr sources, and
`fmristore` adds HDF5. A storage package adds its own format by implementing
a handful of generics; frames, views, binding, block planning, persistence,
and hashing then work with it unchanged.

This vignette builds a complete source backed by an `.rds` file and checks
it. The file format is deliberately trivial, so the protocol is the whole
lesson.

```{r}
library(fmridataset)
```

## The protocol

An array source is an S3 object with class `c("<your_class>",
"array_source")` and methods for these generics:

| Generic | Returns |
|:--------|:--------|
| `source_shape()` | Two integers: the number of observations and features |
| `source_dtype()` | The storage type, such as `"float64"`, `"float32"`, `"int16"`, or `"logical"` |
| `source_chunks()` | Two positive integers no larger than the shape: the natural read block |
| `source_capabilities()` | Distinct strings, including `"block_slice"` and `"serializable"` |
| `source_fingerprint()` | One string identifying this description and revision of the array |
| `source_open()` | A handle inheriting from `"array_source_handle"` |
| `source_read()` | An observations-by-features matrix for the requested positions, in order |
| `source_read_native()` | A native spatial object, or an error if the source has none |
| `source_close()` | Releases a handle; descriptors have a default that does nothing |

The package builds `source_descriptor()`, `validate_array_source()`,
`source_realization_cost()`, `content_hash()`, and `check_array_source()` on
top of these; you do not implement them.

Two rules hold the design together.

**A descriptor is not a handle.** The source object holds only plain values
that can be serialized: paths, shapes, types, sizes, timestamps.
It holds no open connections, environments, external pointers, or functions,
and `validate_array_source()` rejects one that does. Open files belong in the
handle that `source_open()` returns.

**Fingerprints are cheap and content hashes are explicit.** The fingerprint
is computed once, when the source is created, from the descriptor's fields
and any evidence you can observe without reading values, such as a file's
size and modification time. It must never hash the array. Identity by value
is `content_hash()`, which the package computes by reading through your
`source_read()` method.

## An RDS-backed source

The constructor reads the file once to learn its shape, records the file's
size and modification time as revision evidence, computes the fingerprint
with the package's canonical hash, `canonical_sha256()`, and validates the
result.

```{r constructor}
rds_source <- function(path, chunks = NULL) {
  path <- normalizePath(path, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  values <- readRDS(path)
  if (!is.matrix(values) || !is.numeric(values)) {
    stop("rds_source() requires a numeric matrix.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  shape <- as.integer(dim(values))
  chunks <- pmin(as.integer(chunks %||% shape), pmax(1L, shape))
  info <- file.info(path)
  out <- structure(
    list(
      path = path,
      shape = shape,
      dtype = "float64",
      chunks = chunks,
      size = as.numeric(info$size),
      mtime = as.numeric(info$mtime)
    ),
    class = c("rds_source", "array_source")
  )
  fields <- c(list(type = "rds_source"), unclass(out))
  out$fingerprint <- canonical_sha256(fields)
  validate_array_source(out)
}

`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x
```

The descriptor methods return stored fields.

```{r accessors}
source_shape.rds_source <- function(x, ...) x$shape
source_dtype.rds_source <- function(x, ...) x$dtype
source_chunks.rds_source <- function(x, ...) x$chunks
source_capabilities.rds_source <- function(x, ...) {
  c("row_slice", "column_slice", "block_slice", "serializable")
}
source_fingerprint.rds_source <- function(x, ...) x$fingerprint
```

Opening checks the file against the evidence recorded at construction. If
they differ, the descriptor is *stale*: the file opened fine, but it is not
the file the descriptor describes. Callers distinguish that from a genuine
I/O failure, so raise each with `source_error()`, which gives the condition
the class callers test for: `type = "stale"` here, `type = "io"` when the
backend fails.

```{r open}
rds_assert_fresh <- function(x) {
  info <- file.info(x$path)
  actual <- list(size = as.numeric(info$size), mtime = as.numeric(info$mtime))
  expected <- list(size = x$size, mtime = x$mtime)
  if (!identical(actual, expected)) {
    stop(source_error(
      paste("RDS file changed since the source was created:", x$path),
      type = "stale", source = x$path, expected = expected, actual = actual
    ))
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

source_open.rds_source <- function(x, ...) {
  rds_assert_fresh(x)
  structure(
    list(source = x, values = readRDS(x$path)),
    class = c("rds_source_handle", "array_source_handle")
  )
}
source_close.rds_source_handle <- function(x, ...) invisible(TRUE)
```

`source_close()` is defined on the handle class because that is what gets
closed. This handle holds only a matrix in memory, so there is nothing to
release; a handle with an open connection would close it here.

The `source_read()` generic checks every selector before your method runs,
and passes it on in one form: `NULL` for the whole axis, otherwise distinct,
in-range, positive positions in the requested order, possibly none. Logical
masks, negative positions, and repeats never reach the method, so it can
index directly. Reading from an open handle is the real implementation;
reading from the descriptor opens, reads, and closes.

```{r read}
source_read.rds_source_handle <- function(x, observations = NULL,
                                          features = NULL, ...) {
  rows <- observations %||% seq_len(nrow(x$values))
  cols <- features %||% seq_len(ncol(x$values))
  x$values[rows, cols, drop = FALSE]
}

source_read.rds_source <- function(x, observations = NULL,
                                   features = NULL, ...) {
  handle <- source_open(x)
  on.exit(source_close(handle), add = TRUE)
  source_read(handle, observations = observations, features = features, ...)
}

source_read_native.rds_source <- function(x, observations = NULL, ...) {
  stop("rds_source has no native spatial representation.", call. = FALSE)
}
```

That is the whole source. In a package, register the methods in the
`NAMESPACE` with `S3method()`; in a vignette, defining them at top level is
enough for dispatch.

## Try it

```{r use}
set.seed(4)
reference <- matrix(round(rnorm(30), 2), nrow = 6, ncol = 5)
path <- file.path(tempdir(), "toy.rds")
saveRDS(reference, path)

src <- rds_source(path, chunks = c(2L, 5L))
str(source_descriptor(src)[c("shape", "dtype", "chunks")])
```

Reads honour the requested order, and every selector form works because the
generic normalizes it first.

```{r use-read}
source_read(src, observations = c(6L, 1L), features = c(5L, 2L))
odd_rows <- c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)
source_read(src, observations = odd_rows, features = -1)
dim(source_read(src, observations = integer(), features = 1:2))
```

The source drops straight into a frame. `explain()` reports it, and views
over it read only what they select.

```{r use-frame}
frame <- fmri_frame(
  assays = list(bold = src),
  observations = data.frame(.obs_id = sprintf("t%02d", 1:6)),
  space = index_space(5L, ids = paste0("f", 1:5))
)
explain(frame)
collect_assay(frame[c("t02", "t01"), "f5"])
```

## Check it

`check_array_source()` runs the behavioural laws every source must satisfy
against the source and the matrix it should hold: a valid descriptor, a
serialization round trip that keeps the fingerprint, safe opening and
closing, reads that match the reference for any selection, views that
compose, and a content hash equal to that of an in-memory copy.

```{r check}
report <- check_array_source(src, reference)
report
```

In a storage package, call it in the tests for every source type you ship:

```{r check-test, eval = FALSE}
test_that("rds sources conform to the array-source protocol", {
  expect_no_error(check_array_source(rds_source(path), reference))
})
```

A broken source fails with an error naming every law it breaks. Here the
descriptor smuggles in a function, which would not survive being saved and
reloaded elsewhere.

```{r check-fail, error = TRUE}
leaky <- src
leaky$loader <- function() readRDS(path)
check_array_source(leaky, reference)
```

`counting_source()` wraps any source and records every read that reaches it,
which is how the package certifies that views and binds read nothing until
asked.

```{r counting}
counted <- counting_source(src)
view <- source_view(counted, observations = 1:2)
source_counts(counted)$reads
invisible(source_read(view))
source_counts(counted)[c("reads", "values")]
```

Rewriting the file makes the existing descriptor stale. Its stored
fingerprint does not change, but every read now fails with the stale
condition, and a new descriptor has a new fingerprint. (Setting the
modification time explicitly avoids depending on the file system's clock
resolution.)

```{r stale}
saveRDS(reference * 2, path)
Sys.setFileTime(path, Sys.time() + 60)

tryCatch(
  source_read(src, 1L, 1L),
  fmridataset_error_source_stale = function(e) "stale"
)
identical(source_fingerprint(rds_source(path)), source_fingerprint(src))
```

## Composition comes free

Because the protocol is uniform, the package's compositions accept the new
source without knowing anything about it. `row_sharded_source()` presents
several sources as one array, with named shards, which is how runs and
subjects stored in separate files are bound together.

```{r sharded}
run_1 <- file.path(tempdir(), "run-1.rds")
run_2 <- file.path(tempdir(), "run-2.rds")
saveRDS(reference[1:2, ], run_1)
saveRDS(reference[3:6, ], run_2)

sharded <- row_sharded_source(
  list(rds_source(run_1), rds_source(run_2)),
  shard_ids = c("run-1", "run-2")
)
shard_manifest(sharded)[, c(".shard_id", ".start", ".end")]
rows <- locate_source_rows(sharded, c(5L, 1L))
rows[, c(".observation", ".shard_id", ".local_observation")]
check_array_source(sharded, reference)$passed
```

```{r delarr-note, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = !has_delarr}
note("delarr (>= 0.2.0)")
```

With the suggested `delarr` package, `as_delarr()` wraps any source as a lazy
`delarr` array, whose reads go through `source_read()` under the same memory
budget.

```{r delarr, eval = has_delarr}
lazy <- as_delarr(sharded)
dim(lazy)
```

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(c(path, run_1, run_2))
```

## Checklist for a storage package

- Keep the descriptor serializable; put open files and connections behind
  `source_open()`, and release them in a `source_close()` method for your
  handle class.
- Compute the fingerprint once, at construction, from descriptor fields and
  cheap evidence such as file size and modification time, never from values.
- Raise `source_error(type = "stale")` when that evidence no longer matches,
  and `source_error(type = "io")` when the backend fails.
- Return reads in the requested order, always as a two-dimensional matrix.
  Selectors arrive already checked.
- Run `check_array_source()` in your tests for every source type you ship.

The rules for selectors are recorded in the package's
[selection algebra](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmridataset/blob/main/inst/architecture/ADR-010-selection-algebra.md),
and those for fingerprints and staleness in its
[fingerprint decision record](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmridataset/blob/main/inst/architecture/ADR-009-source-fingerprints-and-content-hashes.md).
